# ENTROPY_SRC Core Module — Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

The ENTROPY_SRC core module is the central datapath and control block for the entropy source IP. It receives raw random bits from an external noise source, validates them with a set of health tests, optionally conditions them using a SHA-3 based conditioner, and delivers entropy seeds to either a hardware consumer or to firmware through the register interface.

The module shall operate in several modes:

- A normal conditioned mode, where tested entropy is compressed into full-entropy seeds.
- A bypass mode, where tested entropy is packed into seeds without cryptographic conditioning.
- A firmware-override mode, where firmware can observe raw tested entropy, insert its own entropy into the pipeline, or control the conditioning operation.

The module shall provide interrupts and alerts for entropy availability, health-test failures, observed-FIFO thresholds, fatal internal errors, and configuration/security faults.

## 2. Reset, Enable, and Disable Behavior

### 2.1 Reset

After reset:

- All output entropy FIFOs shall be empty.
- No raw entropy shall be accepted from the noise source.
- No entropy seeds shall be delivered on the hardware entropy interface or to software.
- Health-test counters, watermark registers, error indicators, and status flags shall be cleared.
- The module shall be in the disabled state.

### 2.2 Enable

The module shall be enabled through a redundantly-encoded configuration field.

- A transition from disabled to enabled shall cause internal health-test counters and pipeline FIFOs to be cleared.
- After the enable transition completes, the module shall begin accepting raw entropy and processing it through the pipeline.
- If the enable configuration value is not a valid encoding, the module shall not enable the pipeline and shall raise a recoverable alert.

### 2.3 Disable

When the module is disabled:

- The module shall stop accepting new raw entropy from the noise source.
- The module shall deassert any output indicating that it is ready to receive raw entropy.
- Health-test counters and watermarks shall be cleared.
- Output FIFOs shall be cleared.
- If a conditioning operation is already in progress, the module may finish that operation internally, but a seed that straddles the disable boundary shall not be delivered to the final output.
- If the module is disabled while waiting for a conditioning halt, the disable shall be internally extended until the in-flight conditioning operation has completed. During this extended-disable period, no new entropy shall be accepted.

## 3. Configuration and Security

### 3.1 Redundant Configuration Fields

All security-sensitive configuration inputs that select operational modes shall be redundantly encoded.

- If a redundant configuration field is in an invalid state, the module shall treat that field as disabled and shall raise a recoverable alert.
- Invalid configuration states shall not cause the module to enter an undefined or unsafe operating mode.

### 3.2 Register Write Protection

The module shall provide a register write-enable output to the register interface.

- This output shall be asserted only when software register updates are permitted.
- It shall be deasserted while the module is enabled, so that security-sensitive configuration cannot be changed during active entropy generation.

### 3.3 Firmware Permission Enables

The module shall receive two permission inputs from an OTP/efuse source.

- One permission enables firmware reads of entropy data.
- One permission enables firmware-override operation.

These permissions shall be treated as asynchronous inputs and synchronized internally before use.

## 4. Raw Entropy Input and Preprocessing

### 4.1 Input Acceptance

The module shall receive 4-bit raw entropy samples from the noise source along with a validity indicator.

- The module shall assert an enable output to the noise source only when it is enabled, not in an extended-disable state, and its input buffer is not full.
- Valid raw entropy samples shall be accepted only while the module is enabled.
- Accepted samples shall be stored in a small input FIFO before preprocessing.

### 4.2 Bit-Selection Mode

The module shall support a bit-selection configuration mode.

- When this mode is disabled, all 4 bits of each raw sample are used as one entropy symbol.
- When this mode is enabled, only one of the four bit positions shall be selected, based on a configuration field. Four consecutive selected bits shall be packed into one 4-bit symbol before health testing.
- In bit-selection mode, seeds produced by the module shall not be labeled as FIPS-compliant, because the effective entropy rate is reduced.

## 5. Health Testing

### 5.1 General Behavior

All entropy symbols that enter the main pipeline shall be passed through the health-test logic before they can be conditioned or delivered.

- Health tests shall be active only while the module is enabled.
- Health-test counters and state shall be cleared on the enable pulse and when health-test alert counters are reset.
- Health-test thresholds shall be selected based on whether the module is operating in bypass mode or conditioned mode.
- A health-test window shall be defined by a configuration value. At the end of each window, the health-test results shall be evaluated.

### 5.2 Threshold One-Way Property

Threshold registers used by health tests shall be one-way.

- High-side thresholds shall only ratchet downward.
- Low-side thresholds shall only ratchet upward.
- Once a threshold has been written, software shall not be able to relax it to a less restrictive value.

### 5.3 Repetition Count Test

The module shall implement a repetition count test to detect long runs of a constant value.

- The test shall monitor each bit stream for consecutive equal values.
- If the run length reaches the configured threshold, a test failure pulse shall be generated.

### 5.4 Repetition Count Symbol Test

The module shall implement a repetition count symbol test.

- The test shall monitor repeated 4-bit symbols.
- If the same symbol appears more times in a row than the configured threshold, a test failure pulse shall be generated.

### 5.5 Adaptive Proportion Test

The module shall implement an adaptive proportion test.

- The test shall count the number of 1-bits in each window.
- The result shall be compared against both a high threshold and a low threshold.
- If the count exceeds the high threshold or falls below the low threshold, a test failure pulse shall be generated.
- The test shall support both aggregate scoring over all bits and per-bit-line scoring, based on a configuration field.

### 5.6 Bucket Test

The module shall implement a bucket test.

- The test shall count occurrences of each possible 4-bit symbol.
- A failure pulse shall be generated if any symbol count exceeds the configured threshold within a window.

### 5.7 Markov Test

The module shall implement a Markov test.

- The test shall count transitions between consecutive symbols, such as same-to-same and same-to-different pairs.
- It shall compare the number of switching versus non-switching transitions against high and low thresholds.
- As with the adaptive proportion test, the Markov test shall support aggregate or per-bit-line scoring.

### 5.8 External Health Test Interface

The module shall expose the health-test datapath to an optional external test block.

- The module shall provide the post-health-test entropy symbols, their validity, clear pulses, active indication, threshold values, window-wrap pulse, and threshold-scope configuration to the external test block.
- The module shall accept external test result counts and failure pulses.
- External test failures shall be accumulated in the same failure counters and alert logic as internal test failures.

### 5.9 Health-Test Failure Handling

Each health-test failure shall increment:

- A per-test failure counter.
- A combined “any failure” counter.
- A total-fails counter for that health test.

The module shall capture high-water-mark values for each test separately for bypass mode and conditioned mode, so software can observe the worst-case statistical behavior.

A failure state shall be latched until the current health-test window completes. The completion event shall be used by the control state machine to determine whether the entropy from that window may continue through the pipeline.

When the combined failure counter reaches the configured alert threshold, the module shall:

- Raise a recoverable alert.
- Assert the health-test-failed interrupt.
- Cause the main control state machine to stop delivering new seeds until the alert condition is resolved.

## 6. Firmware-Override Mode

### 6.1 Activation

Firmware-override mode shall be active only when:

- The OTP/efuse firmware-override permission is enabled.
- The firmware-override mode configuration field is set to a valid true value.

If the firmware-override mode field is invalid, the module shall not enter firmware-override mode and shall raise a recoverable alert.

### 6.2 Observe FIFO

In firmware-override mode, the module shall continuously copy tested entropy into an observe FIFO.

- The observe FIFO shall store 32-bit words.
- The current depth of the observe FIFO shall be readable by software.
- If a threshold value is configured, the module shall assert the observe-FIFO-ready interrupt when the depth reaches or exceeds that threshold.
- If the observe FIFO is full, new data shall be dropped.
- If data is dropped because the FIFO is full, the module shall set an overflow status indication.
- The observe FIFO shall be readable by firmware. Each read shall consume one 32-bit word.
- A read attempted while the FIFO is empty shall be treated as a FIFO protocol error and reported in the error status.

### 6.3 Firmware Entropy Insertion

The module shall support a mode where firmware inserts entropy into the pipeline through a write-data register.

- This mode shall be active only when firmware-override mode is active and the entropy-insert configuration field is valid true.
- In this mode, writes to the write-data register shall be pushed into the pre-conditioner FIFO or bypass FIFO, depending on the active datapath mode.
- A status output shall indicate when the write-data path is full.
- A write attempted while the write-data path is full shall not be accepted, and shall cause a recoverable alert.

### 6.4 Firmware-Controlled Conditioning

When firmware-override insertion is active in conditioned mode, the SHA-3 conditioner shall be controlled by a firmware start field.

- Firmware shall assert the start field to begin the conditioning operation.
- While the start field is asserted, firmware may continue writing entropy words into the pipeline.
- When firmware deasserts the start field, the module shall finish processing any complete pending block.
- If firmware deasserts the start field while the write-data path is full, the module shall raise a recoverable alert.
- In that case, the next two conditioned outputs shall be marked as corrupted and shall not be delivered to the final output FIFO.

### 6.5 Interaction with Normal Pipeline

- If firmware-override mode is active but entropy insertion is not active, tested entropy shall continue through the normal pipeline while also being stored in the observe FIFO.
- If entropy insertion is active, tested entropy from the noise source shall be routed to the observe FIFO, and the pipeline shall be fed from firmware writes instead.
- In bypass mode, firmware writes shall be packed directly into 384-bit bypass seeds.
- In conditioned mode, firmware writes shall be fed into the SHA-3 conditioner.

## 7. Conditioning and Datapath Modes

### 7.1 Conditioned Mode

In normal conditioned mode:

- Tested entropy shall be packed into 64-bit words.
- The words shall be sent to a SHA-3 conditioner configured for SHA3-384 operation.
- The conditioner shall produce one 384-bit seed from a fixed-size block of input entropy.
- The module shall not send data to the conditioner unless the health-test window has not failed.
- The module shall backpressure the previous pipeline stages when the conditioner is not ready to accept data.

### 7.2 Bypass Mode

In bypass mode, the SHA-3 conditioner shall not be used.

- Tested entropy shall be packed directly into 384-bit seeds.
- Bypass mode shall be selected when FIPS-compliant operation is disabled, or when configured to send bypass entropy to software.
- Seeds generated in bypass mode shall not be marked as FIPS-compliant.

### 7.3 FIPS Compliance Flag

Each final seed shall carry a one-bit FIPS compliance flag.

- The flag shall be asserted only when:
  - The module is enabled.
  - The datapath is in conditioned mode.
  - The module is not in bit-selection mode.
- If the flag is not asserted, the entropy consumer shall treat the seed as not FIPS-compliant.

## 8. Final Seed Storage and Delivery

### 8.1 Final Seed FIFO

The module shall store completed 384-bit seeds together with their FIPS compliance flags in a final seed FIFO.

- The depth of the final seed FIFO shall be configurable at instantiation time.
- The final FIFO shall be cleared when the module is disabled.
- If the final FIFO is full, newly completed seeds may be discarded. This dropping is intentional and shall not be reported as a FIFO error.

### 8.2 Hardware Entropy Interface

The module shall provide a hardware interface for entropy seed delivery.

- When the module is configured to route entropy to the hardware interface, it shall respond to a consumer request by presenting a 384-bit seed and its FIPS flag.
- The module shall assert an acknowledge response only when a seed is available and has been consumed.
- If no seed is available, the module shall hold the acknowledge deasserted until a seed becomes available.
- When configured to route entropy to software, the hardware interface shall not consume seeds from the final FIFO.

### 8.3 Software Entropy Interface

The module shall support routing final seeds to software.

- Seeds routed to software shall be unpacked into 32-bit words.
- Software shall read the entropy words one at a time from a read register.
- Each read shall consume one 32-bit word.
- A full 384-bit seed shall be read as twelve 32-bit words.
- Software reads shall be permitted only when:
  - The module is enabled.
  - The OTP/efuse firmware-read permission is enabled.
  - The entropy-data-register enable configuration field is valid true.
- If software reads the entropy-data register when reads are not permitted, the read shall return zero and shall not pop data.
- The module shall assert an interrupt when software entropy words are available and the module is enabled.

### 8.4 Repeated-Seed Integrity Check

The module shall check delivered final seeds for repeated values.

- The module shall remember the previous delivered seed.
- If a newly delivered seed matches the previous seed, the module shall raise a recoverable alert.
- The alert shall indicate a potential entropy datapath integrity problem.
- This check shall be cleared when the module is disabled.

## 9. Interrupts

The module shall support the following interrupt events:

1. **Entropy valid for software**: asserted when unpacked entropy words are available for firmware reads.
2. **Health test failed**: asserted when the health-test alert threshold has been exceeded.
3. **Observe FIFO ready**: asserted in firmware-override mode when the observe FIFO depth reaches its configured threshold.
4. **Fatal error**: asserted when a fatal internal error has been detected.

Each interrupt shall support standard enable, state, and test behavior through the register interface.

- An interrupt output shall be asserted only when the corresponding event is present and the interrupt is enabled.
- Writing the interrupt test bit shall force the interrupt event.
- Software shall be able to clear a pending interrupt state.

## 10. Alerts

### 10.1 Recoverable Alerts

The module shall raise a recoverable alert for the following conditions:

- Any redundantly-encoded configuration field is in an invalid state.
- A health-test alert threshold has been exceeded.
- The main control state machine has entered an alert state.
- A repeated-seed integrity violation has been detected.
- The configured alert threshold and its inverse are inconsistent.
- Firmware attempts to write to a full firmware-override write path.
- Firmware deasserts the firmware-override SHA3 start field while data is still pending.

Recoverable alerts shall be reported through the alert status interface and shall not be treated as fatal.

### 10.2 Fatal Alerts

The module shall raise a fatal alert for the following conditions:

- An internal FIFO write, read, or state protocol error.
- A main state machine sparse-FSM error.
- A hardware-interface acknowledge state machine error.
- A redundant counter error in any health-test, window, or fail counter.
- A SHA-3 state, count, or storage error.
- An error triggered through the error-injection register.

The fatal alert output shall be asserted when any fatal error event is present.

### 10.3 Alert Test Outputs

The module shall provide separate alert test outputs for recoverable and fatal alerts.

- Writing the corresponding alert-test field shall generate a one-cycle alert pulse.
- The test pulse shall follow the same output path as a real alert event.

## 11. Error Reporting and Injection

### 11.1 Error Status Registers

The module shall provide error status bits that are set when internal errors occur.

- FIFO errors shall be reported by source FIFO and by error type: write, read, and state.
- State-machine errors shall be reported separately for the main control state machine and the hardware-interface acknowledge state machine.
- Counter errors shall be reported collectively.
- SHA-3 errors shall be reported as state errors, count errors, and storage-reset errors.

### 11.2 Error Injection

The module shall support an error-injection register.

- Writing an error-injection value shall set the corresponding error status and, where appropriate, assert the fatal alert path.
- Error injection shall not corrupt actual datapath data.
- Error injection shall be available for verification of the error reporting logic.

## 12. Status and Debug Observability

The module shall provide status information for diagnostic purposes, including:

- The current depth of the final seed FIFO.
- The current depth of the observe FIFO.
- The current state of the main control state machine.
- Whether the main state machine is idle.
- Whether the initial boot-phase seed generation has completed.
- The current SHA-3 FSM state.
- Whether the SHA-3 block has processed a block, is squeezing, or has absorbed data.
- Whether a SHA-3 error has been recorded.

This status information shall be observable through the register interface. It shall not affect entropy datapath behavior.

## 13. Output to the Noise Source

The module shall provide a FIPS-mode output to the noise source interface.

- This output shall be asserted when the module is not operating in bypass mode.
- This output shall inform the noise source whether FIPS-compliant operation is active.
- It shall not be asserted while the module is disabled.
